title: Should have, must have, could have
goal: Look back at the past with a modal verb: say what you should have done, guess what must have happened, and comfort someone who couldn't have known.
bekal: express regret with *borde ha*, *skulle ha* and *kunde ha* + supine
speculate about the past with *måste ha*, *kan ha* and *kan inte ha*
apologize and reassure in natural Swedish (*Det var mitt fel*, *Du kunde inte ha vetat*)
wave: Go back to Unit 2: say the supine of ten strong verbs (*druckit, skrivit, flugit, burit, tagit…*), then put *borde ha* in front of each one and finish the sentence: *Jag borde ha skrivit till henne.*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — På bryggan
dialogs.intro: Saturday evening on Styrsö. Dian and Oskar have spent the whole day on the warm rocks, swimming and drinking coffee from a thermos. They hurry down to the jetty — just in time to see the boat pull away.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Nej! Där går båten!
lines.id: Oh no! There goes the boat!
lines.literal: no! there goes boat-the!

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Typiskt. Vi borde ha gått från klipporna tio minuter tidigare.
lines.id: Just our luck. We should have left the rocks ten minutes earlier.
lines.literal: typical. we ought have gone from rocks-the ten minutes earlier.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Förlåt, det var mitt fel. Jag skulle ha kollat tidtabellen ordentligt.
lines.id: Sorry, it was my fault. I should have checked the timetable properly.
lines.literal: sorry, it was my fault. I should have checked timetable-the properly.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Äsch, jag kunde också ha kollat. Och jag ville ju bada en gång till.
lines.id: Oh, come on, I could have checked too. And I was the one who wanted one more swim.
lines.literal: pooh, I could also have checked. and I wanted of-course bathe one time more.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: När går nästa då?
lines.id: So when's the next one?
lines.literal: when goes next then?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Om en timme och tio minuter. Jag trodde att de gick oftare på lördagar.
lines.id: In an hour and ten minutes. I thought they ran more often on Saturdays.
lines.literal: in an hour and ten minutes. I thought that they went more-often on Saturdays.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Du kan ha tänkt på sommartidtabellen.
lines.id: You might have been thinking of the summer timetable.
lines.literal: you can have thought on summer-timetable-the.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Ja, det måste ha varit det. Den slutade gälla förra veckan.
lines.id: Yes, that must have been it. It stopped running last week.
lines.literal: yes, it must have been that. it stopped apply last week-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Då hinner jag knappast hem innan sju. Mamma väntar på mitt samtal.
lines.id: Then I'll hardly make it home before seven. Mom is waiting for my call.
lines.literal: then have-time I hardly home before seven. mom waits on my call.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Du kan ju ringa henne härifrån. Hon skulle säkert gilla utsikten.
lines.id: Well, you can call her from here. I'm sure she'd like the view.
lines.literal: you can of-course ring her from-here. she would surely like view-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Du har rätt. Det borde jag ha tänkt på själv.
lines.id: You're right. I should have thought of that myself.
lines.literal: you have right. that ought I have thought on self.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Och sedan köper vi en glass. Det finns sämre ställen att vänta på.
lines.id: And then we'll buy an ice cream. There are worse places to wait.
lines.literal: and then buy we an ice-cream. there are worse places to wait on.

notes: **Vi borde ha gått** — *borde* (ought to, should) + *ha* + supine looks back at something that **didn't** happen and should have. It is the standard way to express regret or mild criticism. English "should have" is the exact match.

**Jag skulle ha kollat** — *skulle ha* + supine is another "should have", with a slightly different flavor: it points to something that was planned or expected of you. *Jag skulle ha ringt dig* can mean "I was supposed to call you" (and didn't). Both *borde* and *skulle* work in Dian's sentence.

**Jag kunde också ha kollat** — *kunde ha* = could have: a possibility that existed and wasn't used. Oskar shares the blame politely, a very Swedish move. The little *ju* in the next sentence means "after all, as we both know".

**Du kan ha tänkt på…** — careful: **present** *kan ha* means "may have, might have", a guess about what actually happened. **Past** *kunde ha* (above) is about a missed chance. *Han kan ha glömt* (Maybe he forgot) vs *Han kunde ha dött!* (He could have died — but didn't).

**Det måste ha varit det** — *måste ha* = must have: a confident conclusion about the past, exactly like English. *Den slutade gälla* — *sluta* + infinitive (no *att*) means "stop doing": *Jag slutade röka*.
**Knappast** (**KNAHP-pahst**) — "hardly, barely": *Det hinner vi knappast* (We'll hardly make it). Pronounce the *k* — Swedish never drops it before *n*, unlike English *knife* or *know*.

grammars.title: Looking back with regret
body: The pattern is the same for every modal: **modal + ha + supine**. The modal is usually in the past (*borde, skulle, kunde*), and the result talks about something in the past that **didn't** happen.

head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: should have (was supposed to); would have
could have (same, a bit more emphatic)
Vi **hade kunnat** ta den förra båten.
Du **hade inte behövt** ta med kaffe.

after: **In speech, *ha* almost vanishes.** *Skulle ha* sounds like **SKÜL-lah**, *borde ha* like **BOOD-dah**. Some speakers even drop it completely: *Jag skulle kollat.* Recognize this, but always write *ha*.
*Hade kunnat* and *hade behövt* already contain the supine (*kunnat*, *behövt*), so they are followed by a plain **infinitive**: *Vi hade kunnat **ta** båten*, not *ha tagit*.
Full "if I had…, I would have…" sentences come in Unit 14. For now, note that *skulle ha* can mean "would have" on its own: *Hon **skulle ha gillat** utsikten* (She would have liked the view).

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Mejlet som försvann
dialogs.intro: Monday morning at the office. Karin has just had a phone call from the client in Borås, and she doesn't look happy.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Dian, kunden i Borås säger att de inte har fått skisserna.
lines.id: Dian, the client in Borås says they haven't received the sketches.
lines.literal: Dian, client-the in Borås says that they not have got sketches-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Va? Jag skickade dem i onsdags, innan Mattias gick på sitt möte.
lines.id: What? I sent them on Wednesday, before Mattias went to his meeting.
lines.literal: what? I sent them in Wednesday, before Mattias went on his meeting.

lines.speaker: Mattias:
lines.text: Jag fick dem i alla fall. Mejlet kan ha hamnat i deras skräppost.
lines.id: I got them, anyway. The email may have ended up in their spam folder.
lines.literal: I got them in all cases. email-the can have landed in their junk-mail.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Det kan det. Eller så var filerna för stora. Hur stora var de?
lines.id: It may have. Or else the files were too big. How big were they?
lines.literal: it can it. or so were files-the too big. how big were they?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ungefär trettio megabyte. Jag borde ha skickat en länk i stället.
lines.id: About thirty megabytes. I should have sent a link instead.
lines.literal: about thirty megabyte. I ought have sent a link in place.

lines.speaker: Mattias:
lines.text: Ingen fara. Det har hänt mig också. Du kunde inte ha vetat att deras system är så gammalt.
lines.id: Don't worry. It's happened to me too. You couldn't have known their system is so old.
lines.literal: no danger. it has happened me also. you could not have known that their system is so old.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Precis. Men nästa gång ringer vi och dubbelkollar.
lines.id: Exactly. But next time we'll call and double-check.
lines.literal: exactly. but next time call we and double-check.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ska jag ringa dem nu och be om ursäkt?
lines.id: Shall I call them now and apologize?
lines.literal: shall I ring them now and ask about excuse?

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Ja, gör det. Och skicka en länk den här gången.
lines.id: Yes, do that. And send a link this time.
lines.literal: yes, do it. and send a link this here time-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Nu har jag pratat med dem. De hade inte ens tittat i skräpposten!
lines.id: I've talked to them now. They hadn't even looked in the spam folder!
lines.literal: now have I talked with them. they had not even looked in junk-mail-the!

lines.speaker: Mattias:
lines.text: Där ser du. Då skulle de ha hittat det på två sekunder.
lines.id: There you go. They would have found it in two seconds.
lines.literal: there see you. then would they have found it on two seconds.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Nåja, nu vet vi. Bra att du ringde direkt, Dian.
lines.id: Oh well, now we know. Good that you called right away, Dian.
lines.literal: well-well, now know we. good that you rang directly, Dian.

notes: **Mejlet kan ha hamnat i skräpposten** — *kan ha* + supine: a **possible** explanation, not a certain one. Karin's reply *Det kan det* ("It may have") is a typical Swedish short answer: the subject *det* plus the modal, repeated from the question.

**Eller så var filerna för stora** — *eller så* (**EL-ler soh**) = "or else, or maybe". It introduces an alternative explanation, and like any first element it is followed by the verb: *eller så **var** filerna…*

**Du kunde inte ha vetat** — "you couldn't have known": the classic way to take the blame off someone. *Kan inte ha* is its present-tense twin for guesses: *Han kan inte ha sett det* (He can't have seen it). The supine of *veta* is *vetat*.

**Ingen fara** (**ING-en FAH-rah**) — literally "no danger", in practice "No worries, it's fine". With *Det har hänt mig också* (It's happened to me too), Mattias makes Dian feel better in two short sentences.

**Be om ursäkt** (**beh om Ü-shekt**) — "to apologize", literally "ask for an excuse". In speech, *Förlåt* is enough among friends; *Jag ber om ursäkt* is what you say to a client. The *rs* in *ursäkt* merges into **sh**.

**De hade inte ens tittat** — the pluperfect from Unit 1, now with *inte ens* (**IN-teh ens**, not even). And Mattias' *Då skulle de ha hittat det* is "would have": if they had looked, they would have found it.

grammars.title: Guessing about the past
body: When you weren't there and have to work out what happened, use a modal + *ha* + supine. Here the modal is mostly in the **present** (*måste, kan*), because the guess is made now.

head: How sure?
Pattern
Example
English
rows: The email may have ended up in spam.
They would have found it right away.

after: Compare the present-tense guesses you already know: *Han **måste vara** sjuk* (He must be ill) → *Han **måste ha varit** sjuk* (He must have been ill). Add *ha* + supine and the guess moves into the past.
In a subordinate clause, BIFF puts *inte* before the modal: *Jag tror att han **inte kan ha** sett det.* More natural still: *Jag tror inte att han kan ha sett det.*
Unit 6 adds softer guesses about the future with *lär*, *antagligen* and *troligen*.

head: About now
About the past
English
rows: He must be / must have been at home.
She may be / may have been ill.
It can't be / can't have been true.
You should call / should have called her.
We could take / could have taken the boat.

blocks.text: The right-hand column is always built the same way: keep the modal, add *ha*, and turn the verb into the supine. If you know your supines from Unit 2, you already know every form in this unit.

blocks.title: Saying sorry — and making someone feel better
items: *Förlåt, det var mitt fel.* — Sorry, it was my fault.
*Jag ber om ursäkt.* — I apologize. (formal)
*Jag borde ha tänkt på det.* — I should have thought of that.
*Ingen fara!* / *Det är lugnt!* — No worries! It's fine!
*Du kunde inte ha vetat.* — You couldn't have known.
*Det kan hända vem som helst.* — It could happen to anyone.

blocks.text: *Krångla* is the everyday word for anything that won't work as it should: *Skrivaren krånglar igen* (The printer's acting up again). The noun *krångel* means hassle, and *krånglig* means complicated — three useful words for life with machines and with bureaucracy.
